title: Empirical Thresholding for Automatic Fallback and Circuit Breaker Activation
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Implement a data-driven thresholding engine that triggers automatic fallback (regional/tier cutover and model-variant fallback) and circuit-breaker actions based on empirical signal distributions rather than static heuristics. This ticket covers design, implementation, telemetry, and an initial canary rollout plan.

Background: We currently use hand-tuned thresholds (fixed 429 counts, static error-rate percentages, and hard timeout windows) to flip routing behavior and open soft circuit-breakers. These thresholds lead to either premature failovers for short-lived anomalies or slow reaction to sustained degradations. For Dedicated and Private customers with strict SLAs, we need a tenant-aware, statistically grounded approach that adapts to baseline traffic patterns and sequence-length distributions.

Scope:
- Build an "Empirical Thresholding Engine" (ETE) service that ingests short-window histograms for per-route signals: 429 rate, 5xx rate, p95/p99 latency, timeout counts, and per-tenant token/req rates.
- Compute per-route and per-tenant dynamic thresholds via rolling quantiles and change-point detection (configurable windows: 1m, 5m, 15m).
- Expose a simple policy DSL to map threshold crossings to actions: soft-fallback-to-variant, regional-cutover, degrade-to-embeddings, open-circuit with cooldown.
- Integrate with the router to gate fallback activations via a two-stage decision (observe -> validate -> actuate) to avoid flapping.
- Implement tenant probation and decay windows: after an activation, require decay period and probabilistic retries before full restore.
- Telemetry: emit activation events with context (signal snapshot, historical baseline, decision confidence score), and surface them in Console rollout dashboards.

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- Statistical method: prefer rolling quantiles + EWMA for baseline and CUSUM for sustained shifts. We considered z-score-based alerts but quantiles are robust to heavy tails in token/response distributions.
- Reaction aggressiveness: default to conservative (favor detection of sustained degradations) but make per-route policy tunable for latency-sensitive vs cost-sensitive tenants.
- Validation step: add brief probing (two synthetic requests to fallback target) as a cheap canary before global actuation, to reduce false positives from noisy ingress spikes. Probing will be rate-limited and simulated for privacy in Private deployments.
- Data retention: keep 1h high-granularity windows, 7 days aggregated. Avoid long retention to reduce cost and PII surface.

Rollout plan:
1) Internal canary (api-team routes only) with monitor-only mode that writes activation suggestions to a bucket and Console timeline. 1 week.
2) Soft-actuate for low-risk routes (embeddings/re-ranking) for select tenants, with immediate rollback TTL=5m. 2 weeks.
3) Broader rollout with tenant-aware cooldown and opt-out flag exposed to customers. 3 weeks.

Telemetry and observability:
- New metrics: ete.activation_attempts, ete.activations_success, ete.decision_confidence (histogram), ete.probe_latency, ete.reason_code (tagged).
- Traces: attach ETE decision trace to sample requests that triggered activation for end-to-end debugging.
- Dashboards: add per-region per-route activation stream and a drift heatmap showing deviation from baseline quantiles.

Open questions:
- How aggressive should automated retries be after transient network flaps? Proposed default: exponential backoff with randomized jitter, max 3 attempts.
- For multi-variant fallbacks, should we apply weighted gradual traffic shifts or immediate cutover? Proposal: staged rollout (10/30/60/100) over a 5-20 minute horizon depending on confidence score.

Links and artifacts:
- Design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/ETE-Design (draft)
- Prototype PR (router integration): https://github.com/redwood-inference/router/pull/1207
- Canary dashboard (Grafana): https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/ete-canary

Acceptance criteria:
- ETE service computes thresholds in prod-like canary with <=2s decision latency for 99% requests.
- Router accepts ETE decisions via gRPC endpoint and performs validation probe before actuation.
- Console surfaces activation events and clients can opt-out per-route.
- No increase in customer P95 latency during canary beyond 0.5% relative baseline (measurement window).
